ascend.hardware_scope: Ascend 910C / A3; runtime, model, input and component combinations determine validation scope

commands.accuracy: model and selected module numeric comparisons; optional A100 oracle
commands.performance: total/layer latency, throughput, allocator memory, independent profiler and telemetry; optional A100 baseline
commands.preview: bounded grouped candidate search and current-identity joint policy validation
commands.export: CPU-only preparation and first fixed batch native graph for supported models; no accelerator initialization or device mounts
commands.report: read-only performance views, filters, portable copying and bounded profiler reanalysis
commands.oracle: native A100 single-device precision reference with independent repeat validation
commands.performance-baseline: native A100 single/TP2 independent performance reference
commands.analyze: CPU analysis and comparison recovery in a new directory; no device recapture
commands.repack-reference: read-only historical reference conversion to a new core and evidence attachment

preview.verified_meaning: selected functions executed, hit and passed finite boundary checks for the current identity; not business accuracy or hardware-kernel qualification

monitor.scope: independent device-management and worker CPU/RSS telemetry; capability and valid points reported per metric

result_retention.ordinary_success: compact when execution and analysis complete without numeric or measurement-review anomalies

limits: listed model adapters only; no task/business scoring
DeepFM/DLRM use synthetic weights and inputs; no CTR/AUC claim
TP parameter support is not qualification of every scale and component combination
OneRec comparison stops at the first selected-token divergence including that step; later trajectories retained
eager execution may not call the Triton compiler
FlagCX lifecycle is scoped to one-shot workers
call-level routing does not prove hardware-kernel fallback coverage
execution changes require a new preview; historical reports and reference packages remain readable
layer parent/child inclusive windows and allocator peaks are not additive
cross-vendor NCCL kernel and CANN collective times are not directly ratio-comparable
compact results cannot recover discarded tensor or raw profiler evidence
polling interval does not define sensor refresh rate or short-batch attribution
short functional validation does not establish stable performance or business accuracy
